title: Constructing Types with Builders
goal: Use the builder pattern to construct complex types with safe defaults and optional parameters.

sections.text: In Java or Python, constructors often use optional arguments or method overloading. Rust does not have default arguments or function overloading, so complex types use the builder pattern.

sections.caption: Method chaining builds a configuration step by step.

sections.text: The builder struct holds temporary configuration state. Each builder method consumes `self` or borrows `&mut self` and returns `self` or `&mut self` to allow chaining.
Consuming `self` by value in builder methods prevents re-using a partially configured builder in an invalid state.

sections.caption: By-value builder methods consume and return Self.

sections.text: The final `build()` method consumes the builder and returns the finished type, validating all fields before returning.

explanation: Use the builder pattern to construct complex types with safe defaults and optional parameters.
